evals.prompt: I've got an APK at ~/Downloads/game.apk — decompile it into something I can edit and then recompile back into an installable APK.
evals.expected_output: Decoded smali+resource tree produced; apktool b recompiles cleanly (clean exit = success); rebuilt APK signed and the signer's own signature check passes (v1/v2/v3), so it is installable; success is judged by the tools' exit codes plus install/run, NOT by re-decoding the rebuild and diffing it against the original; honest note that a bit-identical APK is impossible without the developer's signing key and that this doesn't matter for a working rebuild.

evals.prompt: Change the displayed app name of this APK to something custom, rebuild it, and confirm the new name is actually baked into the rebuilt APK.
evals.expected_output: res/values/strings.xml app_name (or the manifest label) edited; apktool b + sign succeed; aapt2 dump badging on the rebuilt APK shows the new application-label.

evals.prompt: My rebuilt APK won't install — adb says INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE. What's wrong and how do I get it onto my emulator?
evals.expected_output: Explains signature mismatch vs the already-installed (differently-signed) build; instructs adb uninstall <package> then adb install of the debug-signed APK; references troubleshooting.md.

evals.prompt: The interesting logic in this app is in a native .so, not the Java. Decompile the native library and figure out whether it can be recompiled back into a working library.
evals.expected_output: Uses objdump/radare2/Ghidra (via the native subcommand / GhidraDecompile.java) to disassemble/decompile the .so; explains decompiled C is one-way; demonstrates the reassemblable-disassembly round-trip with native-roundtrip.sh (ddisasm + gtirb-pprinter) producing a functionally-equivalent .so, and is clear it is not byte-identical.

notes: Skill is APK-agnostic; these prompts use placeholder paths. Success is defined by the toolchain's exit codes (apktool b + signer succeed) plus install-and-run behavior — there is no re-decode/diff 'verify' step, since that only re-tests apktool's own fidelity, not the user's edit. Validated end-to-end on a real published game APK: edited smali recompiled and signed cleanly, installed, and ran with the change in effect. Native round-trip (native-roundtrip.sh) is a separate path: ddisasm reassembly is genuinely unreliable (unlike apktool/aapt2), so its load-and-run check is a real sanity test, not toolchain self-test.
